newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends softer, eyes 1,000-per-mark peg.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends softer, eyes 1,000-per-mark peg.

text.p: The lev closed at 977-978 per mark, down from the opening's 975-977, as demand for marks rose on the local interbank market ahead of upcoming currency board peg to the mark from July 1, dealers said.
* Traders adjusted lev/mark exchange rates to the pending 1,000-per-mark peg and the current central bank main lev interest rate, now set at 47.28 percent annually.
* The lev fell to 1,672-1,678 per dollar at the close from the morning's 1,669-1,672, tracking the local lev/mark rate and the mark/dollar cross on international markets.
* The lev will be pegged to the mark at a fixed exchange rate of 1,000 under a currency board system, to be launched from July 1.

* Trade was brisk as some banks and clients were offering foreign currency for levs to lock in discount government securities amid expectations that the main interest rate will fall sharply under a currency board system.

* Bids were received for some 62 billion levs at Wednesday's auction of Bulgaria's Finance ministry issue of 18 billion lev worth of four week discount T-bills. The issue was sold out at an average accepted price of 97.49 percent of par, yielding 2.57 percent to maturity.
* Dealers expected local currency to ease by 1.2 levs per mark daily on the average this week to match the peg rate by July 1. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
